summary.intent: Take on the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony: analyze the supplier data drops, find where the launch plan hides problems, then build and polish a product (Lighthouse) that rechecks the plan and acts on it, ahead of a 12:00 hand-in and demos.
summary.outcome: Found that the Collector's Edition misses Sunday despite an 'all ok' plan (80,000 vs 8,000 art-book receipt, failed statue lot, magnet false alarm, game cards short), then built a polling/agent pipeline and web app. The UI work covered roles, Maren's All open tab, Fixed today, a case flow ('How we got here') and routine step fixes, with most work committed on main (360 tests pass) but main not pushed after the last push and live not restarted.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no webhooks or notifications. The only way to see changes is polling the file list and comparing SHA-256 checksums, since existing files are replaced under the same name.

Confidential portal data lives in the gitignored data/ folder and .env; .env.example is the only committed variant. Entire only checkpoints when repo files change, so read-only turns show 'no files modified'.
The API does not load .env on import, so new settings such as ASK_VIEWER_TITLE must be read through a helper that loads .env first, or they go missing after restart.

Routine steps are only valid for certain watch kinds: 'Chase once if no answer' needs routines watching messages awaiting a reply, and 'Ask for a status' needs shipment routines. The server rejects them on decision routines with 'step 2 cannot be done on open decisions'.
Case flow reuses the routine diagram's connector and node components exported from FlowGraph.tsx so both are drawn by the same code.

Lucas's new-approach branch contains a separate pulse-console app with its own escalation loop and email sending that would bypass the duplicate-send guard and record-only demo mode. Only its 'read new documents before verification' step is worth porting into runner.run_pipeline, keeping the no-model skip and try/except safeguards.

Work on separate branches runs in sibling worktree folders (../ask-soony-pulse, ../ask-soony-flow). Merging a branch into main is what makes it visible on live and the demo after a rebuild, while new server endpoints need a restart.
Team workflow is in CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md; a Now line must be claimed in PROGRESS.md before starting a task.

code.finding: New 'How we got here' component. It reads each node from the case's own data (agent steps, evidence, prediction, approval rule, options), omits steps with no data, and ended up as a single top-to-bottom column because the two-column snake read right-to-left.

Pulse-style 'Describe it' chat on branch jonas/pulse-ui. It was merged then reverted because it duplicated the existing 'change in your words' box and was not what the team liked about Pulse; the branch is parked.

friction: Several user requests were misread and had to be redone: roles replaced names instead of being added, Maren got 'Ask Maren to approve' on her own cases, and a second chat was built when the flow view was wanted.
The two-column snake layout of the case flow, the small-screen empty spacing and the overlapping action bar required repeated redesigns.
Initial 'Fixed today' logic read supplier reply fields and wrongly listed Boise's late 36,000 game cards; it had to be rebuilt from confirmed-orders data.
The 'Add step' menu offered steps that the server rejected, which looked like a bug to the user.
Time pressure: many UI fixes landed in the last 15 minutes before the 12:00 hand-in, with main still unpushed.
Portal credentials were pasted into chat, which put them in Discord history.
open_items: Push main (about 13 commits ahead of origin after the last push) and restart live so sign-in choice, Maren's 'Waiting for your OK' and the heartbeat appear there.
Make 'All cases' show the case list directly on phones (just started, last screenshot not reviewed).
Port 'read new documents before verifying' from Lucas's new-approach branch into runner.run_pipeline, with safeguards and testing on a state copy.
Restructure the Routines page into a compact list with details on demand, a ⋯ menu for Run/Delete/Show code, and duplicate-routine detection.
Support 'send email, then chase once if no answer' on decision routines via a reply-watching follow-up.
Choose a Lighthouse logo from the four variants being drawn by a subagent.
Prepare the pitch deck and video, and optionally add a document preview inside the flow nodes.
Register sender email addresses in the portal and send the real Karton Nowak art-book order (24 h offer) and the Boise EXW reply; check whether supplier replies create portal files.
Rotate the portal password that was shared in chat after the hack.
Delete or keep the earlier Claude doc now that the briefing page exists, and update the briefing page with the 14:37 drop.
